data.narrative:
Applied Intuition, a Series F AI & Software company, is evaluated against a comp universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir). The target's last reported valuation of $15.0B was deemed unreliable given it exceeds 20x the company's $600M+ total raised, suggesting a data integrity issue in the source.

Stage-progression valuation was excluded due to this sanity check failure. The peer-median method is applicable and anchors the analysis: across 8 same-sector, similar-valuation-tier peers, the median valuation is $12.0B, with a range of $3.2B (low) to $39.0B (high). The comp set includes Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Scale AI ($29.0B, Series B), Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Skild AI ($14.0B, Series C), and Crusoe Energy ($10.0B, Series C).

Triangulation across applicable methods yields a valuation range of $10.2B to $13.8B, with a median of $12.0B. The compressed range reflects reliance on a single method; key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations ($3.2B–$39.0B), stage heterogeneity across the comp set, and the absence of profitable public AI software peers for direct margin or revenue multiple calibration. Material upside or downside depends on whether Applied Intuition's revenue, customer concentration, or unit economics differ materially from the peer median.
